page: Microsoft Azure HX176-24rs is a High Performance Computing instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system allocates 24 dedicated Intel vCPUs alongside 1408.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory density of approximately 58.67 GB per core. The instance includes hardware support for RDMA networking and compatibility with Azure Premium Storage, while containing zero discrete GPUs.

Local physical storage is supplied via an integrated 4355 GB NVMe solid-state drive, enabling high-throughput and low-latency temporary data caching directly on the host node. External networking configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating routed or private cloud networking infrastructure.

The hardware configuration features an extreme memory-to-core ratio, prioritizing massive memory capacity over raw parallel processor counts. This architectural tradeoff makes the instance suitable for memory-constrained scientific modeling, large-scale in-memory database processing, high-throughput batch analysis, and RDMA-interconnected distributed nodes requiring expansive working memory per thread.
